headline: Video Games Keep Minds Sharp, Study Shows
meta_description: Research reveals gamers outperform non-gamers on cognitive tests and show brain aging 13.7 years slower.
summary_short: A new study found that frequent video game players scored better on cognitive tests and were cognitively 13.7 years younger than non-gamers.
body:
Frequent video game players scored better on several cognitive tests compared to non-gamers, according to a new study. Most striking: the gamers were found to be cognitively 13.7 years younger than those who don't play.

The research adds to growing evidence that gaming offers more than entertainment. While earlier studies have explored links between games and mental performance, this finding puts a specific number on the potential benefit—suggesting that regular gameplay may meaningfully slow cognitive aging.

The study marks a shift in how researchers view gaming, moving past concerns about screen time to examine genuine cognitive gains. For millions who already enjoy video games, the research offers reassurance that their hobby supports brain health alongside its entertainment value.
quick_facts: Frequent gamers scored better on multiple cognitive tests
Gamers showed 13.7 years less cognitive aging than non-gamers
